column1: # Donkey Kong Bananza (Switch 2, update v458752). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive), SDK 20.5.19, NVN2 (the Switch 2's NVN: Ampere shaders, DLSS); modules main + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/, updates/<version>/, dlc/) with scripts/pack_dump.py. Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code).
# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (not measured here): with the guessed Switch 1 pool (3.2 GB) the game's heaps did not fit (AudioSystemHeap creation returned null, main+0x564b48).
# 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 9 GB heap region
# The NPDM declares no system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, and the game sets a heap (without the key the host answers 32 MB, and the SDK's VammManager
# asks GetInfo 0x21, which Switch 1 kernels do not have, for the size to map up front)
# agl's render buffer binding wraps its clears in render conditions (SetRenderEnableConditional(RENDER_IF_NOT_EQUAL) at main+0x12798c before the ClearColor at main+0x1279d4):
# without the key, a clear-only rebinding of the composite target right after the composite draw wiped it before the upscaler read it, and every gameplay frame came out black

# Dynamic resolution (MaintainGpuPercentage: the NDSR rate between NdsrUpscaleMinRate and NdsrUpscaleMaxRate) reads the GPU time between the frame's timestamp reports: each report takes its segment's GPU start / end
# The window size (the nvnWindow textures the upscaler's output is copied to; the render targets scale with it) is the constant pair two leaf functions of main return (mov w0,#2880 / #1620; ret):

# the host writes DM_WINDOW_SIZE's size into them at load (loader.c window_apply; the Android launcher's Game resolution: Phone 1080p = 1920x1080), the game's own 2880x1620 without it (the game note, Window size)
# The game advances its world by the frame rate sead's frame-rate controller hands its framework, 60 / the interval it picked, from one sdiv (v458752 main+0x204b20,
# v0 main+0x1eadf0). With this key the rewriter gates that sdiv (v458752's place is an OBS row of patches.py, any other build's found by its code) and the host makes
# the rate the measured one there, so the game keeps its speed at any frame rate (dm/tools/nso_code.py sead_find, hle_fpslock.c sead_rate). The key also tells the launcher
# the game's speed follows the measured rate: a frame limit (60/45/40/30/20) with presentation on the host's own tick instead of 60/30/20 locking
# The dynamic resolution controller (MaintainGpuPercentage), for the Android launcher's Dynamic resolution setting (probe.c drs_install): where the host finds the
# range's parameter object (ldr x8, [x10, #0x5d0]), where every path's pick meets before it is stored (ldr x9, [x19, #0xf0]), the GPU budget load (ldr s2, [x19, #0xe8])
# and a preset's automatic flag (ldrb w8, [x20, #0x29]). The row also tells the launcher the game has the setting
# DM_FASTBOOT=1: A every 12 presented frames (0.1 s held) from the first present through the boot screen, the title, Continue and the file, a [mark] once 5 frames in a row

# have 3,000 draws or more (the title has 63, the loading screen 6-9, the first level 5,500 and more) and no presses after it. With the seed save, am start to the first level in 45-50 s on the PNM-N49
